reason: The text narrates a clear case of the men of Shechem (Hebrew people) complaining about and rebelling against their leader Abimelech. Initially they make him king, but after God sends an evil spirit between them, they betray him (וַיִּבְגְּד֥וּ בַעֲלֵי־ שְׁכֶ֖ם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ). Gaal explicitly questions Abimelech's authority, asking 'Who is Abimelech and who is Shechem that we should serve him?' (מִֽי־ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ וּמִֽי־ שְׁכֶם֙ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֔נּוּ). The people curse him (וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ), set ambushes against him, and ultimately rebel against his rule, leading to violent conflict.
